title: Integrating AI with RPG Maker MZ for Educational Games

posts.author: AimanHalim
posts.body:
Hello everyone,
I'm exploring the possibility of integrating AI with RPG Maker MZ to create an educational game for my students to learn English. I have a couple of ideas and would love to hear your thoughts on their feasibility:
AI Companion
: An AI character that follows the player, providing guidance, explanations, and answering questions.
Dynamic Content Generation
: AI integration to generate in-game questions and evaluate the player's answers.
Has anyone attempted something similar or have any insights on how to achieve this? Any advice or resources would be greatly appreciated!
Thank you!

posts.author: Ms Littlefish
posts.body: Pre-modded to inform everyone to stay on the topic at hand and discuss the question. Resist the roller coaster.

posts.author: TheAM-Dol
posts.body:
@Trihan
was working on something that could be implemented, but I think last I heard the company providing the API changed there terms that might have stopped it's RM implementation dead in the water.
Due to AI having limited "tokens" for free members you'd either have to take a loss and pay for user's tokens, implement a way for the game to inform users they are out of tokens, or require users to pay monthly (which they would be paying the AI company not you)
Regardless, as a language educator myself, I think making targeted questions for your students level would be far more valuable. You *can* use AI to assist you. I've used it plenty to help me structure lessons better or help me quickly come up with vocabulary, writing prompts, listening prompts, and tests that meet the needs of my students. And this way you are still fully in control, since the end product has to be implemented by you, you can vet the output to ensure it is accurate and adequately matches the needs of your students. I would not solely trust the output of AI without vetting of it's output, especially in a curriculum.

Thanks for the detailed response,
@TheAM-Dol
! You've hit on some of the exact concerns I had about token limits and payment models, which definitely make it a tricky proposition for a free game.
I really appreciate your perspective as a language educator.
You've given me a lot to think about regarding targeted questions and how AI can be a
tool
to assist, rather than the sole driver. I've actually started exploring ways to use AI more in the background for content generation (like vocabulary or prompts) that I can then vet and implement myself. That way, I maintain control and ensure accuracy, which is paramount for educational content.
